jess: Heads-up - new users hitting a 404 from the python quickstart. README points to `getting-started/async_sample.py` but that path doesn't exist on main (looks like we moved the folder). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-examples/blob/main/getting-started/async_sample.py  :grimacing:

nate: Confirmed. We renamed `getting-started` -> `onboarding` last sprint and missed this README reference. I'll open a small PR to update the links.

aiya: Also noticed the async snippet that *is* in the docs is causing runtime confusion. Example shows:
```
from redwood import Client

async def demo():
    async with Client(api_key=\"...") as c:
        await c.generate(\"hi\")
```
That errors for new users with: `TypeError: 'Client' object is not an async context manager`. The runtime Client is the sync variant, AsyncClient isn't exposed at package root so users import the wrong symbol.

jess: Ouch. That will be really confusing for people copying the snippet. Do we intentionally expose AsyncClient somewhere else?

nate: Right now AsyncClient is implemented in `redwood.async_client` and isn't exported in `redwood/__init__.py`. Quick fix is to export AsyncClient or update the docs to `from redwood.async_client import AsyncClient`. Prefer exposing at package level for discoverability.

aiya: There's also a typing mismatch in the distributed stubs (.pyi). The stubs say `Client` is a protocol that covers both sync/async methods, but the runtime default is sync-only. MyPy users get "SyncClient instance has no attribute '__aenter__'" or similar errors depending on strictness. We should make AsyncClient explicit in the stubs so the typechecker matches runtime symbols.

jess: Good catch. Can we make the examples show both usages and a note? e.g. show `from redwood import Client` (sync) and `from redwood import AsyncClient` (async) and include a comment that `Client` is not awaitable or usable in `async with`?

nate: Agreed. I'll prepare PRs for: (1) fix README link, (2) export AsyncClient in package init, (3) update quickstart examples to import AsyncClient explicitly and include both sync/async variants, (4) adjust stub files so mypy can infer AsyncClient when used.

aiya: One more related thing: auth/retry section in the quickstart shows `retry_on_401=True` expecting token refresh to be attempted automatically. Customers report that hosted API will *not* auto-refresh customer-managed tokens; that behavior is only available in Dedicated/private with `enable_auto_refresh=True`. The quickstart should call that out or show an example refresh callback for hosted users.

jess: Yes, a short footnote in the auth section would help. Maybe also show a tiny retry wrapper snippet for hosted users that re-requests a token and retries once.

nate: I'll bundle the doc clarifications into the same PR as the example fixes. Also adding a test case for the sample snippets in CI.

jess: About CI - can we add a lightweight link-checker GH action for the python-examples repo (or a repo-wide md link check) so future path renames fail CI? I can add the markdown-link-check action if folks approve.

docs-bot: Created issue #4290: "python-examples: fix async sample import, update stubs, clarify auth-refresh semantics, add markdown link CI" and assigned to @nate. (automated)

aiya: Minimal repro that I pasted into the issue for the async context problem:
```
# repro_async_bug.py
from redwood import Client

async def main():
  async with Client(api_key=\"tok\") as c:
    await c.generate(\"test\")

# -> TypeError: 'Client' object is not an async context manager
```

jess: Nice repro. Nate, can you also add a changelog bullet for the quick fix so we can surface it in the next patch release notes?

nate: Yep - will add CHANGELOG entry and ping @sdk-owners for review on the stubs change. Planning to land the link fix today and the AsyncClient/stubs docs tomorrow.

jess: Thanks. Anyone wants the stub patch, ping aiya for review.

aiya: Happy to review.

jess: OK closing thread — follow-ups in #4290.

End of thread.
